en.title: Tekken 8 Drops Baki's Yujiro Hanma in Early 2027 Season 3 DLC
en.summary: The King of the Land, Yujiro Hanma, is officially joining the Tekken 8 roster as a Season 3 DLC fighter. Get ready for the ultimate showdown when he arrives in early 2027.
en.body:
The iron fist of **Baki the Grappler** is about to collide with the King of the Iron Fist Tournament. Bandai Namco has officially confirmed that **Yujiro Hanma**, the overwhelmingly powerful father of Baki himself, will be the next major addition to **Tekken 8** as part of its Season 3 DLC. While a precise release date remains elusive, the studio has pegged his arrival for early 2027, leaving fans to eagerly anticipate the full reveal.

This monumental crossover was teased during Evo France 2026, alongside a more substantial look at other upcoming **Tekken 8** DLC content. While the trailer showcased the return of beloved characters like Roger Jr., the brief glimpse of **Yujiro Hanma** at the very end sent shockwaves through the community. Capturing the sheer, terrifying presence of the "Ogre" in the hyper-realistic engine of **Tekken 8** is no small feat, and early impressions suggest Bandai Namco is embracing his signature, almost inhuman, physicality. Fans have long speculated about a **Baki** character joining the **Tekken** universe, and **Yujiro** is arguably the most iconic and fitting choice, embodying raw power and a chilling charisma that should translate exceptionally well into the fighting game arena.

## The Uncanny Valley of Hanma

The initial teaser, while short, focused on **Yujiro Hanma**'s most recognizable traits: his intimidating smile and his almost supernatural flexibility. Fans are buzzing with anticipation, dissecting every frame of the brief appearance. The challenge for the developers is immense; **Yujiro**'s character design in the **Baki** series is known for its exaggerated musculature and expressive, often monstrous, facial features. Translating this into **Tekken 8**'s established aesthetic, which leans towards a more grounded, albeit still stylized, realism, is a delicate balancing act. Early reactions online indicate a mix of excitement and a touch of apprehension, with many wondering if the in-game render will truly capture the terrifying aura of the anime's ultimate antagonist or fall into the uncanny valley. The promise of a full gameplay trailer premiering alongside the **Tekken** World Tour Finals on January 17, 2027, will be crucial in alleviating these concerns.

## Community Hype and Anticipation

The inclusion of **Yujiro Hanma** is more than just another DLC character; it's a dream crossover for many fighting game and anime enthusiasts. **Baki** has a dedicated global fanbase, and **Yujiro** stands as its formidable figurehead. His raw power and unique fighting style are expected to bring a fresh dynamic to **Tekken 8**'s already diverse roster. The community is abuzz with speculation about his move set, potential rage arts, and even his taunts. The fact that this is the first time a **Baki** character is officially entering a major fighting game franchise only amplifies the excitement. Fans are eager to see how **Yujiro**'s legendary "unarmed fighting" prowess will be represented against **Tekken**'s established martial arts masters.

## What's Next

While **Yujiro Hanma** is slated for an early 2027 release, the **Tekken** World Tour Finals on January 17, 2027, will serve as the stage for a brand-new, in-depth trailer. This upcoming showcase is expected to finally reveal **Yujiro**'s official release date and provide a comprehensive look at his gameplay mechanics, potentially putting an end to much of the community's speculation.

content_raw: Bandai Namco has revealed a first look at Tekken 8 DLC character Yujiro Hanma, and the Baki rep is looking just as uncanny as fans expected. The new trailer for the fighting game's Season 3 characters debuted alongside Evo France 2026. Following Kunimitsu's release in June and Bob's release in August, kangaroo-and-joey fighter Roger Jr. is now officially set for a November 11 early access launch, with the full release following November 16, but the character most fans are looking forward to is still without a proper release date. Roger Jr. is definitely the star of the new Tekken 8 DLC trailer, with nearly three minutes of its four-minute runtime dedicated to showing off the marsupial boxer's gameplay. The Yujiro teaser, meanwhile, is tucked at the end, but its reveals are particularly shocking. You can see how the Baki the Grappler villain has been reimagined within the world of Tekken below. Yujiro is… expressive, to say the least, so nailing his face and bulging muscles was always going to draw attention. Well, the Bandai Namco team did their best, with today's Evo trailer showing just a few shots of his iconic toothy smile and flexibility. It looks like work on the anime guest character is still underway, but just because there's no release date doesn't mean there isn't a plan to show more. The end of the new teaser promised that a new Yujiro trailer will premiere alongside the Tekken World Tour Finals January 17, 2027. That's three months out from now, so we can probably expect to see gameplay by that point. Looking back at the calendar, Bandai Namco has typically had a few months of downtime between Tekken 8 DLC releases. It will have been two months since Roger Jr. was released when the Yujiro trailer is shared, meaning we can also expect a release date announcement around that time, too. If we're lucky, the Baki fighter might even drop that same day, but again, nothing regarding his release date has been confirmed quite yet. Roger Jr. and Yujiro are both included in the Season 3 pass and will round out its promise of four bonus characters. Season 1 and Season 2 included fighters like Heihachi, Armor King, Anna, and Final Fantasy 16 protagonist Clive Rosfield. While passes cost $30 each, the Season 3 pass is currently available for $34.99. IGN learned more about Yujiro's inclusion in Tekken 8 when speaking with producer Naoya Yasuda and director of promotions and former Baki manga editor Yuki Yokoi earlier this year. Be sure to read the full interview for insight into how and why the team decided to include a character that never loses. You can also read about how former Tekken director Katsuhiro Harada influenced one of Roger Jr.'s best references , and the player who climbed through the ranks while blindfolded .
